title: The Wood Knock
logline: Every night at 3:12 AM something knocks three times on the apartment door, and nobody is ever there. Barney blames a woman he jilted for the moon, Marshall blames an urban Sasquatch, Ted blames a woman too in love to finish a sentence, Robin wants a gun, and Lily, who knows exactly who it is, hides it very badly.

guests.name: Gretchen
guests.role: A cheerful night-shift ER nurse who once had half a dinner in Bermuda with 'Ted Mosby, astronaut' (Barney), has just moved onto the block, and has not thought about him once since

guests.name: Celeste
guests.role: The Woman at the Door, entirely Ted's invention: a breathtaking architect who has memorized his thesis on load-bearing walls and is too in love with him to wait after she knocks

facts.lily.family_plans: trying for a baby with Marshall; Marvin told everyone
facts.lily.dad: reconciling with Mickey: he knocks three times, she knocks three back
facts.lily.favorite_game: Home by Bedtime, Mickey's two-player game nobody can lose
facts.barney.alias: told Gretchen, a nurse on the block, he was Ted Mosby, astronaut

opens.note: Mickey and Marshall start designing a Sasquatch board game called Wood Knock at 3:30 AM

scenes.label: 3:12 AM
scenes.summary: Dark apartment. Three knocks. Ted, armed with an umbrella, and Marshall check the door: nobody, for the fifth night. Marshall wants to knock back (wood-knock etiquette, runner 1); Lily stops him far too fast and blames a punctual wind. Everyone goes back to bed except Lily, who stays at the window looking down at the street.

beats.line: Marshall. Did you hear that?
Fifth night in a row. Ted, this is how every documentary I own starts.
Who's there?
Nobody. Again. Just the hallway and Mrs. Matsuda's doormat that says Go Away.
Okay. Stand back. I'm knocking back.
Why would you knock back?
So it knows we're friendly.
So what knows we're friendly?
Exactly.
Marshall, don't!
Lilypad?
It's the wind. Wind knocks. That's a wind thing.
Lily, the wind doesn't knock at exactly 3:12 every night.
It's a very punctual wind. Bed. Everybody.
You coming, Lilypad?
In a minute.

scenes.summary: The theories. Ted parses three knocks as a question. Barney: Gretchen, whom he ditched mid-dinner in Bermuda as 'Ted Mosby, astronaut', has moved onto the block and is scorned. Marshall: Bigfoot-adjacent, wood knocks, and his imagined triumph on Metro News One. Lily over-endorses Bigfoot, which moves Marshall to tears and makes Ted suspicious; she threatens him with the cloak. Robin: gun. Ted: a woman too in love to wait after she knocks (dream cutaway). Robin calls it his dating history. Ted's real point lands on Lily. Stakeout tonight; Lily will be asleep near it.

beats.line: By the sixth night, all five of us had a theory. Well. Four of us.
Six nights. 3:12 every time. Three knocks. People, three knocks is a question. Two is a pizza. Four is the police.
And I know who's asking. Gretchen.
Who's Gretchen?
A lovely woman I met in Bermuda, who believes she had dinner with an astronaut named Ted Mosby.
You used my name?
Ted, you have a trustworthy name. It's your only good quality.
I'd love to stay for the crab cakes, Gretchen. But the moon needs me.
Will you call me?
Every night. From space. Look up. I'll be the twinkly one.
And last month, Gretchen moved onto our block. I saw her at the deli. She saw me. She bought a cruller.
Angrily.
So a woman knocks on Ted's door every night because you stood her up for the moon.
Hell hath no fury, Robin, like a woman scorned for space.
Or. And hear me out. It's not a woman. It's not even a man.
Marshall, if you say Bigfoot—
I'm not saying Bigfoot.
I'm saying Bigfoot-adjacent.
Out west, Sasquatches talk by knocking on trees. It's called a wood knock. Ted, what is our door made of?
Oak veneer over particle board.
Wood, Ted!
And when I prove it, I'm gonna be on the news.

beats.label: Metro News One, any day now

beats.line: Tonight, a Sasquatch has been found living in a rent-stabilized two-bedroom on the Upper West Side.
Marshall Eriksen, how did you do it?
I just knocked back, Robin. Respect. That's all he ever wanted.
Remarkable. And you were right about the moon landing.
I know.
I think it's Bigfoot.
You what?
Bigfoot-adjacent. Totally. It's science.
Lily. In nine years, you have never once let me have Bigfoot.
Well, I'm growing as a person.
Lily, last night you said it was the wind.
And I loved Barney's theory too. All theories are great. Let's never test any of them.
You're being weird.
Ted. Drop it, or everyone finds out about the cape.
It's an opera cloak!
Or. Gun. Chair facing the door. I solve it tonight.
Robin, no guns. Not in the apartment, not near the apartment.
Fine. No guns.
Besides, I have a theory. Someone gets to our door every night with something to say, and loses their nerve.
Someone like who?
A woman. A beautiful, brilliant woman. Probably an architect.
Ted Mosby. I've read your thesis on load-bearing walls. Twice.
Tonight I knock. Tonight I tell him he's the one.
Tomorrow. I'll tell him tomorrow.
So your theory is a woman so in love with you, she runs away.
Yes.
Ted, that's not a theory. That's your dating history.
The point is, it's not random. Three knocks, then they wait. That's somebody waiting for an answer.
So tonight, we stake it out. Marshall and I take the door.
Barney and I take the sidewalk. Nobody gets into that building without us seeing them.
And when Gretchen shows, I'll let her down easy. Suited. Women love closure almost as much as astronauts.
And I'll be asleep.
Lily, it's a stakeout!
I'll be asleep near it.

scenes.label: 2:58 AM
scenes.summary: Inside. Ted's umbrella is practically a sword; Robin took the actual sword. Marshall will knock back (runner 2); Lily, 'asleep' on the couch, forbids it. Ted notices Lily hasn't asked a single question all week. Lily says the word snore. Marshall defends her.

beats.line: Ted. You brought an umbrella to a stakeout.
It's a steel-shafted British umbrella. In the right hands, it's a sword.
We have actual swords.
We have one sword. Robin took the other one.
Here's the plan. When it knocks, I knock back.
You will not.
Lilypad? Are you awake?
No.
Marshall, Lily hasn't asked one question about this all week. She asks questions about everything.
She asked our mailman if he was happy. He wasn't. They talked for an hour.
Snore.
She's exhausted, Ted. Twenty kindergartners. That's like sixty regular people.

scenes.summary: Outside. Robin has the sword: Ted only banned guns. Gretchen comes up out of MacLaren's after her shift. She remembers Barney fondly as Ted Mosby, astronaut, and isn't scorned at all. Barney can handle hated; he can't handle fine. Robin: how was the moon? Barney: lonely.

beats.line: You brought a sword to a stakeout.
Ted said no guns. He didn't say anything about the stuff on his walls.
Robin, you cannot stand on a Manhattan sidewalk at three in the morning holding a sword.
Three guys have walked by. Not one of them asked for my number.
That's because of the sword.
I know. Best night I've ever had on this street.
Gretchen. Twelve o'clock.
It's three o'clock.
Oh my gosh. Ted? Ted Mosby?
Hello, Gretchen. I suppose you're here to knock.
Knock? I just got off a double shift. I'm a nurse. I live right there.
How was the moon?
Busy.
I always wondered if you made it! I tell people I dated an astronaut. Well. Half a dinner.
So you're not scorned?
Scorned? Ted, you left halfway through the crab cakes to go to space. Best excuse I've ever heard.
Is that a sword?
Neighborhood watch.
Love this neighborhood.
Robin, I've been hated on four continents. I can handle hated.
I have never been fine.
How was the moon, Ted?
Lonely.

scenes.label: 3:11 AM
scenes.summary: Phone check: nobody has gone in since midnight. Marshall: then it lives here. Silence. The knock. Marshall raises his knuckles; Lily says don't, walks to the door and knocks back, three times. Three knocks answer, and Mickey Aldrin comes in. Ted explains the umbrella badly. Mickey got past the sidewalk by saying excuse me twice (replay: he stood at the stoop the whole time). Lily: Hi, Dad.

beats.line: Status.
Nobody has gone into that building since midnight. Nobody.
Also, Gretchen's fine. Totally fine. Everyone is fine.
Nobody came in. So it's not coming tonight.
Or it's already in the building. Ted. It lives here.
Wood knock. Okay. Here I go.
Marshall. Don't.
Lily, it's etiquette.
I know it is.
Hi, kiddo.
Mickey?
So it's not a Sasquatch.
Not since the eighties.
Ted. Why are you holding an umbrella?
It's for weather.
Inside?
It's a very old building.
Mickey, how did you get past Barney and Robin? Robin has a sword!
The guy in the suit was being let down easy by a nurse. The blonde was laughing at him. I said excuse me twice.
Hi, Dad.

scenes.label: 3:13 AM
scenes.summary: Barney and Robin, who heard nothing from the street, congratulate themselves: no knock tonight, nothing gets past them. They give it fifteen minutes before going up to take credit.

beats.line: 3:13. No knock. Robin, we did it.
We didn't do anything. We stood here.
We stood here magnificently. Nothing gets past us.
Nothing.
Give it fifteen minutes. Then we go up and take all the credit.
I want it on record that the sword did most of the work.

scenes.summary: Lily explains their knock (memory, then the replay years later without her answer). Mickey knew she was awake. Why now: Marvin told him they are trying for a baby, in his Christmas letter, in July. A kid deserves a grandpa who comes through the door. Home by Bedtime: you can't lose anymore. Two players. The hug, left alone.

beats.line: Lily. How did you know to knock back?
Because that's our knock. When I was little, he got home late. Every night.
He'd knock three times on my door. And if I was awake, I'd knock three times back.
Night, kiddo. I'm home.
Then I got older. And he got home later. And I stopped knocking back.
I knew you were awake. You snore when you fake it. Same as your mother.
I wanted you to know what waiting felt like.
Well. I found out.
But why now, Mickey?
Your dad told me you two are trying for a baby.
My dad told you?
Marvin told everybody, son. It was in his Christmas letter. In July.
I figured a kid deserves a grandpa who comes through the door. So I came to the door.
Every night I knocked, and nobody knocked back. And I thought, she's still mad. Which is fair.
I am still mad.
Which is fair.
I made you something.
It's a board game, isn't it.
It's called Home by Bedtime. You're the dad. You have to get home before the little girl falls asleep.
Can you lose?
Not anymore. I took out the racetrack.
And the bar. And the card game. Turns out, without those, it's pretty easy to get home.
It's two players. I couldn't make it work with one.

scenes.label: 3:30 AM
scenes.summary: Barney and Robin knock and come in armed. Robin is glad Ted banned guns; Barney is no longer an astronaut; Ted asks if Mickey read his thesis. Marshall claims the wood knock; Mickey turns it into a board game at 3:30 AM, finally on time for something, and Lily sits down to hear the pitch. Penny and Luke recognize the game.

beats.line: Okay. Nobody came in. So either it's a ghost, or it's somebody who already—
Who's the old guy?
My dad.
Oh. Hi, Mr. Aldrin.
Good call on the guns.
Hey. You're the astronaut.
Not anymore.
Someone at the door every night, losing their nerve before saying something important. I called it.
You said it was a beautiful architect who'd read your thesis.
Mickey, have you by any chance read my—
No.
And Lily knocked back. Wood knock etiquette. You knock back so they know you're friendly.
Wood knock? What's a wood knock?
Oh, Mickey. Sit down.
Sasquatches knock on trees. If you knock back, the Sasquatch knows you're a friend.
Son. That's a board game.
That's a board game!
Dad, it's three-thirty in the morning.
I know. I'm finally on time for something.
Fine. Start from the top.
Wait. Is Home by Bedtime that game at Aunt Lily's where nobody can lose?
I thought it was just a really bad game.
It's a terrible game. It's her favorite.
